lab_title: The Human Heart: Structure and the Path of Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers of the heart and describe their spatial relationships
Locate and name the four heart valves and explain their role in preventing backflow
Identify the major vessels entering and leaving the heart and distinguish oxygenated from deoxygenated blood pathways
Trace the complete dual-loop (pulmonary and systemic) circulation driven by the heart
Explain the structural and functional reason the left ventricle has a thicker myocardium than the right

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the intact 3D heart in anatomical position and orient the student to external landmarks before internal structures are explored.
key_visuals: A life-sized rotating 3D model of an intact human heart shown in correct anatomical orientation
Subtle exterior highlights marking the anterior surface, apex, and base
A floating orientation compass indicating superior/inferior and left/right
student_actions: Rotate and zoom the heart model to view it from anterior, posterior, and lateral angles
Tap the apex and base to reveal short orientation labels
Confirm anatomical orientation before proceeding

scenes.brief_purpose: Have students identify the four chambers and understand the division into right and left pumps.
key_visuals: A frontal cutaway of the heart exposing the two atria and two ventricles
Each chamber shaded a distinct color with hidden name labels
A translucent interventricular septum separating left and right sides
student_actions: Tap each of the four chambers to reveal and confirm its name
Drag chamber name labels onto the correct highlighted regions
Note which chambers receive blood and which pump it out

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the great vessels and connect each to its associated chamber.
key_visuals: The heart with the superior and inferior vena cava, pulmonary trunk and arteries, pulmonary veins, and aorta attached and highlighted
Blue coloring for deoxygenated-blood vessels and red for oxygenated-blood vessels
Directional flow arrows on each vessel
student_actions: Tap each vessel to reveal its name and whether it carries oxygenated or deoxygenated blood
Match each vessel to the chamber it connects to
Predict the direction of blood flow in each vessel using the arrows

scenes.brief_purpose: Locate the four valves and establish their function in enforcing one-way flow.
key_visuals: A superior 'valve plane' view showing all four valves from above
Animated valve leaflets opening and closing in a cutaway ventricle
Labels distinguishing atrioventricular (tricuspid, mitral) from semilunar (pulmonary, aortic) valves
student_actions: Tap each valve to reveal its name and location
Watch the valve open/close animation and identify which phase prevents backflow
Answer a check question pairing each valve with the chambers or vessels it sits between

scenes.brief_purpose: Integrate chambers, valves, and vessels into the complete dual-loop circulation.
key_visuals: An animated blood-flow particle stream traveling the full circuit through the cutaway heart
A color transition from blue to red as blood passes through the lungs
A simplified body-and-lungs schematic showing pulmonary and systemic loops
student_actions: Step through the circulation one segment at a time, tapping 'next' at each structure
Reorder a shuffled list of structures into the correct sequence of blood flow
Identify at which point blood becomes oxygenated and re-enters the heart

scenes.scene_name: Why the Left Ventricle Is Thicker
scenes.brief_purpose: Explain the structural-functional relationship between ventricular wall thickness and workload.
key_visuals: A cross-sectional slice comparing the thin right ventricular wall to the thick left ventricular myocardium
A measurement overlay quantifying the difference in wall thickness
A comparison graphic contrasting the short pulmonary loop with the long systemic loop
student_actions: Compare the two ventricular walls and estimate the thickness difference
Match each ventricle to the circulation loop it serves
Explain in a short response why the left ventricle requires more muscle

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate and assess mastery of structures and the full circulation pathway.
key_visuals: An unlabeled 3D heart with numbered pointers on chambers, valves, and vessels
An interactive flow-path builder canvas
A live score/feedback panel
student_actions: Label all numbered structures on the unlabeled heart
Reconstruct the complete path of blood flow from body to lungs to body
Review feedback and revisit any missed structures
